findings.text: Null stdin and a 30 s terminate stop the Add row hanging; a terminated run shows the generic 'Couldn't add msgblast' message. Process captured in asyncAfter may warn under strict concurrency; native CI shows it.
The wrong-key flag is global, so any tailnet peer can trigger the neutral 'An agent sent an old key' line. UI only, not a security issue.
First user switch-on of outside agents also turns on Tailscale listening when signed in to Tailscale; keys and approvals still required; now disclosed in docs/outside-agents.md.

Loopback accepts only when the last X-Forwarded-For entry (the one Serve appends) is a tailnet address; a local process could forge it but still needs a valid key and approval. No App-layer test for this path; forwardedPeer is tested.
featured: ids map to messages:<uuid> only for contacts in state.agents; confirmed no duplicate entries in agents_list. No new send capability.
Deploy the worker before shipping the app: outside* keys fail validation on the old worker and the whole batch is dropped.
After a restart, Set Up rotates the Grok key if Grok was added but never approved, invalidating that unapproved connector. Acceptable.

privacy_scan: clean: only example.ts.net, 100.101.102.103-style samples, RFC1918/1.2.3.4 test inputs and fixed ports; no usernames, tailnet names, keys or secrets
